# Recorded version-7 state

`review.json` holds the `melian.findings` and `melian.verdicts` snapshots that the review code wrote at `ef617de0`, the head of step 17, before step 18, "Resolution per lens and per rule". Both document definitions were version 7. This is recorded output, not a hand-built old shape.

The recording ran in a checkout of that commit, as a Vitest test in `packages/pipeline/test/`. It built a repository with `createRepository()` and two commits. The base held a `melian.yaml` whose tier ran the guardrails alone and which declared two `forbidden-patterns` rules, `focused-test` and `console-log`, the second at P3. It also held `biome.json` and `src/a.test.ts`. The head added the line `it.only("logs", () => console.log(a));` to the test file, added a `resolution` key to `melian.yaml`, and changed `biome.json`. It ran `reviewChangeset` on memory storage with the fake model and no lens, then read both documents through `harness.snapshot` and wrote them with the revision key. No provider, credential or environment file was read.

The three guardrail sightings therefore carry no `guardrail` field: the line that both rules match names its rules only in prose, and the two policy-change notices name their class only in the discriminator. The verdict's findings carry no `decidedBy`. The reopen test in `findings.test.ts` writes these values through version-7 document tokens to SQLite, closes it, and reads and writes them through the current definitions. It also builds the same two commits again and checks that today's guardrails give the same three finding IDs.
